analysis:
The change to QwenVLMTargetExtractionTests.swift is test-only: it adds endOfPromptBoundaryRequiresDensePagedSSD (head lines 337-367). No production code, protocol, key handling, or attestation path is modified, so no trust boundary or asset (A-001, A-003, TB-002, TB-007) changes directly.

The new test pins the behavior of EngineV2Factory.demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens. It expects a non-nil minimum (the store's minEffectiveTokens) only for a dense Qwen model with the paged backend and a real SSD store. MoE, contiguous, nil-store, and contiguous-store cases must return nil. It also checks that demandedCaptureBoundaryMinimumTokens stays nil for dense Qwen.

These assertions relate to the T-041 per-donation gating (adoption bound plus benefit floor), which limits the at-rest surface. The test asserts the floor is kept, so it reinforces the gating. It uses temp fixtures (SSDHybridCheckpointTestFixture) that are removed in defer blocks, and the fixtures hold no secrets.

The remaining test content, including the complete-checkpoint wiring tests, is context rather than part of the changed range (335-366). It exercises tenant-scoped cacheScope, unique receipts, and a runtimeIdentityUnavailable fail-closed state. I saw no regression there.

The actual production change implementing demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens, which would widen the SSD at-rest donations (T-041 detection_hint), is outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should review it in EngineV2Factory+Production and SSDPrefixCache.donate to confirm the floor is not loosened. The patch excerpt is truncated at the end, but the head text is fully visible.
